reading.body:
NTT CH1 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity at its Itasca, Illinois address. Translating that to racks requires an assumption about power density: at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation average, 36 MW supports roughly 3,600 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks. NTT has not published a per-rack density figure for this site, so neither translation is the operator's claim.

Among the 44 Illinois facilities this site has mapped, only 6 publish a megawatt figure. Those 6 sum to 236 MW of published IT capacity. CH1's 36 MW places it second by published capacity among that group, representing approximately 15 percent of the published Illinois total. That rank reflects only what operators have chosen to disclose, not the full capacity of the state.

No certifications beyond the operator's own facility page were present in the structured data provided, so no certification reading can be offered here. The campus sits in the western Chicago suburbs, inside a dense metropolitan grid, which is relevant to power access, but grid interconnection status and available utility headroom for this site are not published in the data this site holds. Whether 36 MW of existing IT load can expand to serve large AI workloads depends on power availability that is not disclosed.
